findings.title: The served HTTP endpoint is an unchecked string, so the adapter POSTs to any allowlisted host/path chosen by process environment
findings.recommendation: In WebsearchAdapter.load_provider, require the resolved endpoint host to be the first entry of policy.allowlisted_hosts; refuse with a named reason otherwise.

findings.title: max_results is model-controlled and unbounded and is forwarded into the outbound request body
findings.recommendation: Add a maximum to the max_results property in the tool schema (script/websearch_adapter:86) and clamp at line 113.

findings.title: The profile egress declaration is pinned but never reaches the adapter process, so the enforced declaration can differ from the recorded one
findings.recommendation: Have McpSourceBuilder pass the profile's validated egress declaration (or its digest) into the child's env, and have WebsearchAdapter.load_policy refuse when its declaration is not the pinned one.

findings.title: credential_shaped_query? and sanitize_result are test-only; the production builder wires neither into the validator or executor
findings.recommendation: Add the websearch branch to McpSourceBuilder#build_validator/#build_executor keyed on config.server_id == WEBSEARCH_SERVER_ID, and assert it on McpSourceBuilder#build; or, if the adapter already covers it, delete the docstring claim at websearch.rb:46-51.

findings.title: EgressCircuit ignores budget_breach:false and still opens after threshold budget breaches
findings.recommendation: Return early without incrementing @failures when the kind is BUDGET_BREACH_KIND and @budget_breach is false.

findings.title: A timed-out search is re-attempted rather than receipt-replayed because the admitted safety is :read_only
findings.recommendation: None; the FX rule is satisfied and :read_only is the correct classification for a search.

findings.title: The MCP descriptor duck-type has no effect_class/read_only? mismatch guard; websearch's own descriptor and source agree by construction
findings.recommendation: None from this row; the owning seam is McpDispatcher#safety, which could read the host descriptor's effect_class instead of asking the source.

blind_spots: The live HTTP provider path was never executed; all probes used injected resolver/connector. The repo records the live path as an operator-gated deferral.

session_nodes.rb and session_graph.rb were grepped for the egress/effect seam but not read end to end; the FX-rule conclusion rests on session_steps.rb, session_effects.rb and the journal safety table.

test/support/agent_smoke_corpus.rb case 18 (the only end-to-end websearch scenario) was read at the wiring level but not executed; it is a benchmark-harness support file, not a test/*_test.rb suite, and it composes its own validator/executor so it cannot resolve F10-SEC-04.
gems/tamoz-mcp/lib/tamoz/mcp/supervisor.rb was read for the circuit_store seam but not line by line; transport-failure handling on the in-process MCP channel is not fully traced.
coordinator_flags: F10-SEC-03 is the egress-side instance of CF05-SEC-01's unsettled profile-to-MCP admission contract; co-dispose rather than count twice
F10-SEC-04 needs an independent challenge: missing production wiring and misleading documentation are both supported by the sources and have different fixes
F10-SEC-01 has no proven attacker in this read-only audit but the profile-pin contract it violates is a direct source fact
